title: Literary evaluation
intro: Evidence-based assistance using your chosen criteria, not an objective literary verdict.
empty: No evaluations yet. Choose a scope and preview it.
selectionOnly: Only the selected passage is sent by default. No automatic surrounding text, secrets or full chapter.
loadSelection: Load saved manuscript and select a passage
sourceSelection: Select the text to evaluate here
selectText: Select a passage from a saved manuscript first.
gapsNotice: Noncontiguous selections are allowed. Omitted chapters remain unread, with no invented transitions.
bookPolicy: Covers each catalog chapter: Final where available, otherwise its current manuscript. Plan-only chapters are excluded. Full-text segments are read before chapter and cross-chapter synthesis. Any unread target prevents a final book score.
normalization: Overall = Σ(applicable score × weight) / Σ(applicable weights). N/A and insufficient evidence are excluded, never scored as zero. Applicable dimensions remain visible.
rubricSaved: Personal rubric version saved. Existing evaluations retain their frozen rubrics.
contextNotice: Select only authorized style, theme, clue or logic records. They are evaluation premises, not manuscript evidence. All world data is not loaded automatically.
allowContext: Authorize selected author records for this evaluation (extra passage context)
modelNotice: Uses one routed model by default. A second model adds requests; there is no automatic provider fallback. Repeated runs of one model are not independent consensus.
orderNotice: Reverse changes processing order while preserving chapter positions in synthesis. Order and repeated runs may affect judgments; stability is not assumed.
phaseCount: Per model: {{read}} full-text reading units + {{synthesis}} synthesis units
costNotice: Generation does not start automatically. Characters are not exact tokens; synthesis also includes evidence cards. Unknown prices stay unknown. Each batch requires explicit start, with call limits and existing budget safeguards.
unreadable: {{count}} empty or unreadable targets prevent a complete overall score.
planExcluded: {{count}} plan-only chapters excluded from manuscript evaluation.
created: Evaluation frozen. No model has run yet. Review the batch limit before starting.
stale: The manuscript or book catalog changed. This historical evaluation does not describe the current version. Create a new evaluation; history is retained.
noTotal: Coverage or synthesis is incomplete: no final score for the complete scope.
sameModel: These are repeated evaluations by the same model, not independent model consensus.
retry: Retry incomplete requests explicitly (may incur another charge)
working: Processing this batch. Completed units are saved.
chapterNote: Chapter and range judgments are distinct levels; synthesis is not a mechanical average of chapter scores. Gaps are never counted as read.
partialOnly: The following is a partial-subset opinion, not a complete book evaluation or overall score.
judgmentNotice: These are literary judgments within the supplied evidence. Objective language errors, factual conflicts and preferences remain distinct in the existing review system; scores never become Canon.
todoSaved: Revision todo saved through the existing author workbench. Manuscript unchanged.
noteSaved: Note saved without rescoring or penalties.
comparisonNotice: Compares independently saved evaluations. Scope, rubric, order and model differences are flagged. Anonymous A/B hides table labels only; it is not a blinded independent experiment.
notTrend: Different conditions: not a direct quality trend
batchBound: Batch call limit must be an integer between 1 and 20.
passageScore: Local scores for the selected passage
passageNote: These scores describe only the selected passage, not the complete chapter or book.
chooseSecond: Explicitly select the second reviewer model. Choosing the same model repeats evaluation, adds calls and is not independent consensus.
warning_DIFFERENT_APPLICABLE_DIMENSIONS: Applicable dimensions or normalized weights differ; overall scores are not a direct quality trend.
